newsitem.title: SPAIN: Mexico approves extradition of ETA suspect to Spain.
newsitem.headline: Mexico approves extradition of ETA suspect to Spain.

text.p: Mexico agreed on Saturday to extradite a suspected member of Basque separatist rebel group ETA to Spain in a move Spanish officials hailed as a sign of cooperation between the two countries.

"Everything that means collaboration, as long as it's fully legal, for better conditions in the fight against terrorism, will always be judged positively by the Spanish government," Labour Minister Javier Arenas told journalists.
A federal judge in Mexico ruled in favour of the extradition of Oscar Cadenas, alias "El Guero", who was arrested last December on a warrant issued by Spain, a court source said.

The decision coincides with an official visit by Spain's king and queen to Mexico. King Juan Carlos, in a speech quoted on state radio, thanked Mexico for its support in the fight against ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom).

"I want to thank this Senate for its commitment and backing in the fight the Spanish authorities are waging against terrorists that has converted the prolongation of their murderous activity into their only reason for being," the king said in an address to the Mexican Senate.
Cadenas is wanted in Spain on charges of attempted murder, causing criminal damage and belonging to an armed band. He has also been named as a suspect in a 1995 kidnapping by ETA.
Mexico extradited three other ETA suspects to Spain last year after a visit by Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar.
ETA has killed some 800 people since starting a drive for Basque independence in 1968
